sense: give someone a task, a thing or a place

terms.comment: To give someone a share, a charge or a province; Lewis & Short gives tribuō, assignō, dō, ascrībō as its synonyms.

terms.gloss: hand over (a task) to someone else, delegate
terms.comment: Of a charge one would rather not see to oneself (Lewis & Short); good prose, but not in Caesar and perhaps not in Cicero. Not to be confused with dēligō, choose.
The word for allotting public land to settlers; also, generally, to assign or ascribe.

phrases.latin: puerōs attribue eī, quot et quōs vidēbitur
phrases.english: assign him as many slaves as you think fit, and whichever you think fit

phrases.latin: sua quemque māter ūberibus alit, nec ancillīs ac nūtrīcibus dēlēgantur
phrases.english: each is nursed at his own mother’s breast, and they are not handed over to maids and nurses
